verdict.line: You lose if you let him poke you down with Boomerang resets before level 6; you win any all-in you land once Grasp has stacked a shield advantage.

brief.thesis: Sion has zero mana costs and a point-blank kit, so Gnar's entire plan is to whittle him with 1100-range Q (Boomerang Throw) from outside Cryptic Gaze's 550 range while never letting Mini Gnar get caught at melee. The matchup is a dead-even 50% over 96 games because Sion's Grasp sustain and W (Death's Caress) shield can out-heal the poke if he plays the wave patiently instead of chasing it.

theirWindow.when: Rage bar near full, Mini Gnar
theirWindow.what: He is one Q/W/E cast from transforming into Mega Gnar, which brings a stun (W - Wallop) and an AoE slam (E - Crunch). Back off from any trade that would push his Rage to max while you're already low, since the transform itself can swing the fight.

yourWindow.what: The instant he throws Q and whiffs the catch, he has no slow and no poke for up to 16 seconds at rank 1. Walk up, land auto-attacks with E (Enrage) active, and use Q (Cryptic Gaze) to stun him in place if he tries to disengage.

start.why: Picked in 76.9% of these games and winning 54.4% of the time — the flat damage reduction on autos directly answers Gnar's poke-auto-poke pattern, since every Boomerang Throw and basic attack he lands does less.

boots.why: 79.1% pick rate at 51.6% win rate; the attack-speed-based damage reduction specifically cuts down the repeated poke-autos Gnar uses to farm Hyper (W) stacks on you.

core.why: Core first item in the top build path (80% WR over 5 games) — the burn aura punishes him for standing in melee range after any failed all-in.
Second item in both top build paths; the grievous wounds and shield synergize with E (Enrage) trades where you're spending HP for AD.
Closes out the most common build path; the HP-scaling nuke on your abilities turns your passive max-HP growth from kills into real burst in extended fights.

runes.keystoneWhy: The 55.9% page's keystone heals you off every proc, directly countering Gnar's win condition of slowly poking you down with ranged Q before he's forced to commit at melee range.

summoners.why: Run in 90.2% of these games at 53.6% win rate; Teleport lets you reset top after shoving the wave with Enrage (E) autos without surrendering tempo to his ranged poke, and Flash covers your lack of a gap-closer against his 475-range Hop (E).

playing.title: Trade only when Boomerang is down
playing.detail: Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw) is on a 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown and his only ranged tool pre-6. Engage with Q (Cryptic Gaze) and auto-attacks in that window, not while he's holding it ready.

playing.title: Hold Cryptic Gaze for the stun, not poke
playing.detail: Q has a 12/11/10/9/8s cooldown and 550 range — save it to lock him down for a full trade rather than spending it to chip damage from range you don't have.

playing.title: Shield before he commits, not after
playing.detail: W (Death's Caress) absorbs damage and explodes on a timer or on reactivation; pop it the moment he starts a trade so the shield is live for his burst instead of wasted on empty space.

playing.title: Respect the Mega Gnar transform threshold
playing.detail: Watch his Rage bar — at max Rage his next ability flips him into Mega Gnar with a stun (W - Wallop) and an AoE slam (E - Crunch). Don't initiate a close fight right as he's about to cross that threshold.

playing.title: Enrage only when you're committing
playing.detail: E (Enrage) trades your HP for AD on every auto with no cooldown — toggle it on right before you all-in, not while poking at range, since Gnar wins the HP-trade war if you self-damage without landing attacks.

playing.title: Cannibalism for extended skirmishes
playing.detail: R (Cannibalism) leeches HP to you and nearby allies for the duration and boosts attack speed. Save its 90s cooldown for drawn-out fights near your team, not solo duels, since the AoE heal is wasted 1v1.

playing.title: Punish his Mega Gnar landing spot
playing.detail: Mini Gnar's E (Hop) bounces off units to extend his escape; Mega Gnar's E (Crunch) instead slams down in place with no reposition. If he's forced to transform mid-engage, he loses his escape tool — follow in immediately.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being hit with his third (W). Try to gain the upper hand after a couple of pokes.
